planRationale: This broke in the last few days (Axios scoop, Oct 22; CBS follow-up Oct 25) and touches something every non-technical reader has — a bank account — making it immediately relevant. The core lesson (what it means to hand an AI your financial login, and why 'read-only' is the safer middle ground) will remain useful well beyond a month as agentic AI keeps spreading. It fills a clear gap: existing articles cover shopping agents and general account-trust, but none focus on banking and personal money specifically.

findings.claim: Major banks have started restricting third-party agent access over security concerns.
findings.issue: Accurate as of the check date (late October 2026): Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Bank of America, Citi, Wells Fargo and Charles Schwab were reported restricting or blocking third-party AI agents in reports dated October 22-23, 2026. The claim is correct and current, but it is a fast-moving story with no date anchor in the text. The house 'as of <date>' blocking rule is NOT triggered because the content makes no explicit 'as of writing'/'as of today' statement. Consider adding a dated anchor to keep this claim from going stale, since this is exactly the kind of state-of-the-world claim that can be superseded quickly.

items.note: Upload this single file to content/articles/. The existing indexing.yml workflow rebuilds articles_index.json automatically, and the article becomes visible on /trends within a minute or two.

findings.claim: White House AI advisor David Sacks noted there is 'a world of difference between user-authorized agents'...
findings.issue: The quote is accurate and correctly attributed. However, Sacks' title is most commonly reported as 'White House AI czar' (or 'AI and crypto czar'); one outlet referred to him as 'Former White House AI Czar.' 'AI advisor' is a loose but defensible paraphrase and not misleading. Consider using 'White House AI czar' for precision.

findings.claim: JPMorgan already allows this limited approach through data intermediaries like Plaid.
findings.issue: Verified in substance: JPMorgan supports read-only, customer-authorized data sharing through open banking providers, and Plaid is named as an example intermediary in coverage. The specific pairing of JPMorgan + Plaid as a currently-live arrangement is a reasonable characterization but is presented slightly more definitively than sources confirm; sources frame read-only access through approved open-banking providers generally. Not misleading enough to block.
